messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Re: Bayesian SEM or CFA in brms
parts:
Moderatorion is nothing but an interactions (between primary predictor and moderator) from a statistical perspective, so you can easily incorporate those.

Mediation isn't possible yet (you might want to consider the bmlm package for this). It might be implemented in brms as a "byproduct" of more general multivariate models later on this year, but I am not completely sure yet.

messages.author: ed5476e5fee71e9f
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Re: Bayesian SEM or CFA in brms
parts:
You can fairly easily write SEM (e.g. mediation) models in Stan. If you just want to do a simple three variable mediation, that's implemented in bmlm (as Paul suggested): https://cran.r-project.org/package=bmlm

Paul: I'm looking forward to trying out the multivariate models you're thinking of implementing later on. It probably won't be too hard to allow users then to request multiple regression models simultaneously, allowing SEM. If you're able to implement varying effects that identify groups across these models, brms could well become the go-to package for multilevel SEM, which would be nice!

Cheers
Matti
